messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: Spike in 5xx errors from /v1/generate across eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Symptom: latency cliff + KV cache growth. Pager sent to #incidents and oncall.
Jordan (oncall): seeing it. CPU on serving boxes climbing fast, mem pressure, lots of small prefix keys in kv-store. paging latency up to 3s p95. tagging for SRE/ML.
Anya (sre): I can take lead. Any recent deploys to prefix hashing/tokenizer? @Ryan?
Ryan (ml): pushed tokenizer mapping change 6h ago to reduce tokenization variance for templates — shouldn't affect cache keys but the rollout included a small change to prompt normalization (strip whitespace + stable-hash v2). That might change prefix hashes.
Leah (infra): confirm KV store key count jumped from ~40k to 1.2M in last 30m for prefix:layer:prompt-v2:* — looks like thundering creation of tiny keys. Evictions are thrashing.
Jordan (oncall): customers reporting degraded responses. Support started triage.
Maya (support): several high-value customers with production traffic (acct: churn-ops, finx) reported >30% failure on inference calls. Escalated for RCA comms.
Anya (sre): immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle burst creating new prefix keys 2) increase default TTL on prefix cache to avoid constant eviction/repush 3) reduce continuous-batching max_batch_tokens to limit memory pressure 4) rollback prompt normalization in canary if needed. Anyone object?
Ryan (ml): normalization v2 introduced a different token boundary for certain templates; if hashing uses token offsets, keys will diverge. I suggest reverting the hash-version flag in the router to v1 for affected routes first.
Leah (infra): done a quick firewall-style throttle on write QPS to kv-store for prefix:layer:prompt-v2:* -> applying 20% global write cap now. Pushing a config change, will take ~30s to propagate.
incident-bot: change applied by infra-leah; kv-write-qps capped at 20% for prefix:layer:prompt-v2:* (action id ACH-7723).
Jordan (oncall): verifying metrics... number of new keys dropping. CPU slowly trending down but latency still high at p95=1.5s.
Anya (sre): applying TTL bump to 1h (was 5m) for prefix:layer:prompt-v2:* to reduce churn. Command:
```
kvctl set-ttl --prefix "prefix:layer:prompt-v2:" --ttl 3600
```
Leah (infra): TTL change rolled. Eviction rate down 40%.
Maya (support): pinging affected customers: telling them we're mitigating, will update in 30m. No planned customer-facing rollback yet.
Ryan (ml): switching router hash-version to v1 for canary traffic to avoid mismatched prompt hash generation. Patch PR: https://git.internal/redwood/routers/pull/998
Jordan (oncall): canary flip done for 10% traffic -> monitoring traces.
incident-bot: Canary traffic (10%) routed to hash-version=v1 at 1778901499.
Anya (sre): still seeing some perf cliffs — continuous-batching queues are pinning because new requests have a lot of tiny prefixes; recommended reducing max_batch_tokens from 512k -> 128k temporarily. That will increase per-token latency slightly but prevents OOM.
Leah (infra): changed batching config on serving pool eu-west-1 and us-west-2.
Jordan (oncall): after batching change p95 latency back to ~350ms, error rate down to baseline. KV key growth stabilized but total keyspace still inflated.
Ryan (ml): we need a postmortem on why normalization+hash versioning was rolled without dual-write compatibility. Also template drift: some customers had templates auto-updated by client libs which created many near-unique prefixes.
Anya (sre): agreed. Immediate action items captured:
- short term (now): keep kv-write throttle, TTL=1h, batch size reduced, router hash-version canary until keys compact.
- medium (2-12h): run a compaction job to collapse near-duplicate prefixes (heuristic merge), prune very low-hit keys, export list for RCA.
- longer (1-2d): add compatibility mode + feature flag for tokenization/hash changes; enable server-side normalization toggle; create detection alert for sudden key cardinality increases.
Jordan (oncall): on-call handoff in 30m to @Anya for overnight. I'll draft incident summary for post-incident comms.
Maya (support): posting interim status update to customers: "We are mitigating a prefix cache churn issue affecting inference latency. Temporary perf impacts expected to subside in the next hour. No data loss. Follow-up with root cause and timeline tomorrow." :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Leah (infra): kicked off compaction dry-run job on staging to validate heuristics. Command used:
```
kv-compact --prefix "prefix:layer:prompt-v2:" --merge-threshold 0.1 --dry-run
```
Anya (sre): run compaction on prod only after approval from infra-leah and 30m of stable metrics.
incident-bot: MAJOR INCIDENT -> SEVERITY=2 assigned. Playbook: https://playbooks/redwood/kv-cache-churn
Ryan (ml): opened a quick PR to add a hash-version header in router so both client and server can negotiate; link: https://git.internal/redwood/ml/hash-version-negotiation/pull/12
Jordan (oncall): handoff: I'm pausing active watches, Anya taking on-call at 1778901820. I'll be available for quick questions. Key signals to watch: kv-key-count, kv-eviction-rate, batch-queue-length, 5xx-rate /v1/generate.
Anya (sre): acknowledged handoff. Monitoring dashboards pinned. If we need rollback of tokenizer change, Ryan has the PR.
Maya (support): will send a second update to impacted customers in 45m with status and ETA.
Leah (infra): follow-up: we found a small bug in TTL setter that caused inconsistent expiries across zones — fixed in place and re-applied TTL. Patch id infra-ttl-fix-221.
Jordan (oncall): thanks team. Closing active paging once error rate stable for 30m. Leaving incident thread open for postmortem notes.
Maya (support): customers notified: they replied asking about data consistency — confirmed no prompt content altered, only caching behavior.
Anya (sre): next steps for postmortem: timeline, root cause (tokenizer normalize + hash-version rollout + client template churn), mitigation timeline, and concrete code/process changes. Assigning owners: Ryan -> ML fix + flag, Leah -> compaction + infra guardrails, Jordan -> postmortem doc + comms, Anya -> alerting + playbook update.
Jordan (oncall): last check 1778902345: metrics stable. Marking thread as monitoring -> resolved in next 30m if stays green.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: error rate back to baseline, active mitigations in place, severity downgraded to S3 at 1778902345.
